# Remote hosting decision

Checked 2026-11-05; deadline Saturday 2026-11-07 23:59 IST. Estimates below are planning estimates, not provider guarantees.

**Primary: AWS Free plan, Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64 VM with 2 vCPU and 8 GB RAM, if the account and that VM shape are available.** It avoids the pinned Mattermost image's Arm emulation, gives a credible short-term capacity margin, and AWS says most new customers need no payment method. This is credit-funded, not permanent: stop before the credit or six-month limit. Verify the selected EC2 shape, disk, public IP and data transfer are allowed and covered by the displayed credit before launch. AWS availability and account approval are UNVERIFIED. Budget 1.5-3 hours after account activation; allow more for verification and debugging.

**Fallback: Oracle Always Free A1, 2 OCPU / 12 GB Arm,** only if its AMD64 Mattermost image runs acceptably under emulation. Signup needs an accepted card and may place a temporary hold. Home-region capacity and registration can block you. Oracle's current documentation says **2 OCPUs / 12 GB for Always Free tenancies**, despite the larger hourly allowance; do not assume the older 4 / 24 allocation. If Azure for Students is already approved, an eligible x86 8 GB VM on its $100 credit is another good fallback.

**Stay local for the deadline** if no VM and a working four-agent smoke test are ready by Friday evening, signup/capacity fails, or team access cannot be secured and tested. A Windows local server is possible, but persistent SDK agents still need a POSIX SSH host. A WSL/other local POSIX SSH target may be explored, but Switch compatibility and setup are UNVERIFIED; it does not relieve laptop load. Keep the working deployment until migration is proven.

## Primary runbook

1. **Human:** create an AWS account and choose **Free**, not Paid; complete email/phone and any requested identity checks. A payment method is not required for most new customers but may be requested. Confirm $100 credit, Free plan, region, eligible EC2 quota and estimated charges. Do not upgrade to Paid. [AWS terms](https://aws.amazon.com/free/free-tier-faqs/), [Free plan](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/free-tier.html).
2. **Human:** in EC2 launch Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64, choose an eligible 2-vCPU/8-GB shape, 30-40 GB disk and public IPv4; create/download an SSH key. Check all cost estimates and the credit balance. Security group: TCP 22 only from Nikhil's current public IP, updated if it changes; no public 5432, 8000, 3000 or 8065. Add Darshan through Tailscale, not a shared SSH private key. Actual VM price and credit consumption are UNVERIFIED until the portal shows them.
3. On Windows PowerShell, restrict the downloaded key to your user and test, substituting the actual key and IP. Accept the fingerprint only after checking the EC2 host fingerprint through a trusted channel.

```powershell
ssh -i "$env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\labquorum.pem" ubuntu@VM_PUBLIC_IP
```

Add `Host labquorum`, `HostName VM_PUBLIC_IP`, `User ubuntu`, and `IdentityFile ~/.ssh/labquorum.pem` to `%USERPROFILE%\.ssh\config`; confirm `ssh labquorum` works. Ensure the Windows SSH agent is available to Console. On the VM:

```sh
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y git tmux curl ca-certificates
uname -m
free -h
df -h
```

Install Docker Engine and the Compose plugin using [Docker's Ubuntu instructions](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/); check `sudo docker run hello-world` and `docker compose version`. Give the trusted VM user Docker access as described by Docker's post-install documentation; Docker group membership is effectively root access. Reconnect and verify `docker ps`. Install Node 18+ and the Claude CLI through Console host checks or their official installers; install `uv` and clone the authorized repository to the remote user's home. Transfer uncommitted files securely if necessary; do not assume a push is permitted.
4. **Human:** Console > Settings > Remote hosts > Add host `labquorum`; run each prerequisite check/install until Ready. Start a remote server there and register each agent with the remote host and an existing remote working folder. For a separately administered shared Switch deployment, use the pinned Switch repository's Compose deployment instructions and choose a published server artifact version, not the Console release version. Configure `collab` and `gateway`, a stable `MATRIX_SERVER_NAME`, strong unique registration/JWT secrets, and store secrets outside Git. Do not guess a server artifact version. [Self-host guide](https://docs.switchagents.ai/flintai/switch/deploy/self-host).
5. **Human:** sign in to Claude for the same remote OS user that runs the sidecar. On a machine with a browser, `claude setup-token` starts browser approval and generates a one-year token; inject `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` securely into the sidecar's environment, not shell history, a repository or chat. Verify the actual sidecar inherits it and run a real agent request. Use of a subscription token in this exact Switch SDK integration and its applicable terms are **UNVERIFIED**; an API key with separate usage charges may be needed. Authentication is not included in VM free credit. [Claude authentication](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication).
6. Start Mattermost, connect both people, configure personas, folders and the Python MCP server, then exercise four concurrent sessions and a booking. Check `free -h`, `docker stats` and disk; test Darshan's access from his own connection. Back up PostgreSQL, Mattermost data and the SQLite ledger, plus secrets separately. A VM reboot requires restarting the Console-managed server and reopening Console to relaunch the tmux sidecar.

## Two-person access and migration

A public VM alone does **not** share a Console-managed Switch server: it is reached through its owner's Console/host connection. Darshan can use Mattermost if its web service is deliberately reachable and his identity is linked; a shared self-hosted Switch deployment additionally needs Gateway/API addresses and each person needs their own Console and account. [Remote host](https://docs.switchagents.ai/flintai/switch/deploy/host-remotely); [self-host](https://docs.switchagents.ai/flintai/switch/deploy/self-host); pinned `docs/official/getting-started/add-a-server.md:76-104`.

**Fastest private path:** Tailscale on both Windows laptops and VM, restrict access with tailnet policy, and bind/publish only to the private interface or tunnel localhost services over SSH. Check Docker-published ports independently of host firewall rules. No public Mattermost, Switch API, Gateway or PostgreSQL is needed. Verify Mattermost's advertised Site URL, WebSockets, bridge callbacks and Darshan's client actually work. Tailscale account setup and policy details are UNVERIFIED for this team.

**Public alternative:** a DNS name pointing to the VM, Caddy with automatic HTTPS reverse-proxying only to loopback Mattermost, TCP 80/443 open for certificate issuance and HTTPS, and 22 restricted; leave API/Gateway private or put them behind authenticated access. Configure Mattermost Site URL and trusted proxy settings, create both accounts, disable open signup and invitations as appropriate, use strong unique passwords and MFA if available. Verify HTTPS, WebSocket, bridge and signup controls externally. DNS/domain availability and exact configuration for this pinned seeded image are UNVERIFIED. Allow 45-120 minutes plus DNS propagation, domain cost/availability and testing; Tailscale is safer and likely faster. [Caddy HTTPS](https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https), [Mattermost configuration](https://docs.mattermost.com/administration-guide/configure/site-configuration-settings.html).

This is a new host: redo Console host/server onboarding, Mattermost bridge and identities, personas/agent registrations and paths, repo checkout, Python/uv/MCP installation and service credentials. Existing local files and unpushed changes do not appear remotely. Migrate database and secrets only with a verified backup/restore; otherwise rooms/history and ledger start fresh. Console UI stays on Windows; the remote machine runs Switch, database, Mattermost, agent controller, Claude processes and the Python MCP/SQLite ledger. Console can close while they run; host reboot stops the Console-managed stack/sidecar. See `docs/official/deploy/host-remotely.md:7-9,60-64,80-94` and repo `docs/build/switch-facts.md:98-104`.

## Requirements and sizing evidence

Switch specifies Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 Linux or macOS, x86-64 or arm64, SSH public-key auth, sudo or macOS Homebrew, working SSH alias/agent, and Docker for a server; 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 20 GB is a comfortable starting point, not a minimum. Remote checks include git, tmux, provider CLI and Node 18+. `docs/official/deploy/host-remotely.md:15-29,41-46,54-68`. Compose is used for self-hosting; default loopback ports are API 8000, Gateway 3000 and Mattermost 8065, PostgreSQL internal: `docs/official/deploy/self-host.md:52-67`, `deploy/local/standalone-docker-compose.yml:142-152`. SSH is normally 22. Expose only what is needed.

The pinned build publishes switch-core multi-architecture `linux/amd64,linux/arm64` (`.github/workflows/switch-release.yml:254-274`). Console's remote host documentation supports arm64 for the Node sidecar, though successful execution of this exact build is UNVERIFIED. The Compose file pins Mattermost 11.9.0 to **linux/amd64**, explicitly requiring emulation on Arm (`deploy/local/standalone-docker-compose.yml:142-149`); QEMU/binfmt availability and performance on Oracle are UNVERIFIED. Claude Code Linux arm64 support in the exact SDK/CLI combination is UNVERIFIED: test before relying on it.

Mattermost's [official Ubuntu minimum](https://docs.mattermost.com/deployment-guide/server/linux/deploy-ubuntu) is 1 vCPU and 2 GB RAM. Switch's 4 GB starting suggestion is not a four-agent benchmark. Plan **8 GB minimum target, 12 GB preferred**, 30-40 GB disk, as an engineering estimate for OS, containers, four sessions, MCP and headroom; Claude process footprint, simultaneous workload peaks and exact SQLite requirements are UNVERIFIED. Measure rather than assuming 8 GB suffices.

## Candidate evidence and risks

- **AWS:** New accounts get "$100 in credits" and can earn up to another $100; Free plan ends at six months or exhausted credit, with no charges unless upgraded. Most signups need no payment method, though identity checks may request one. x86/Arm shapes and EC2 quota depend on account/region; allow 20-90 minutes plus review, cost and shape availability UNVERIFIED. Strong short-term fit, not permanent. [AWS FAQ](https://aws.amazon.com/free/free-tier-faqs/), [AWS terms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/free-tier.html).
- **Oracle:** A1 Arm allowance is "2 OCPUs and 12 GB of memory" for Always Free tenancies, and 200 GB total block storage; up to two AMD E2.1.Micro instances are too small for this combined load. Credit/debit verification may cause a hold, typically 3-5 days; phone/address required. Account approval 30 minutes to days, capacity UNVERIFIED. Oracle warns "out of host capacity" and Always Free instances must be in the home region. Mumbai and Hyderabad each have one availability domain, so changing AD there is not a workaround; live free capacity is UNVERIFIED. Idle resources may be reclaimed. [Always Free](https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/FreeTier/freetier_topic-Always_Free_Resources.htm), [regions](https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/General/Concepts/regions.htm), [signup/holds](https://www.oracle.com/cloud/free/faq/).
- **Azure for Students:** "$100 in Azure credits" over 12 months, no credit card; 18+, full-time at accredited degree-granting institution and school email verification. Credit exhaustion disables subscription; activation is limited. An eligible x86 VM can fit if quota and credit allow; disk/network consume credit. 30 minutes to days, verification and availability UNVERIFIED. [Offer](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/offers/ms-azr-0170p).
- **Google Cloud:** Always Free is one US-region e2-micro, 30 GB standard disk and limited egress; its 1 GB RAM is unsuitable. Trial offers $300 for 90 days for eligible customers and can fund a larger VM temporarily; card verification/hold and activation delay are possible. Check exact usage and trial eligibility before choosing it. 30-90 minutes plus review. [Free program](https://docs.cloud.google.com/free/docs/free-cloud-features), [trial](https://cloud.google.com/free).
- **GitHub Codespaces:** GitHub Free personal includes 120 core-hours and 15 GB-month: at 2 cores only 60 hours/month. Idle stops after 30 minutes by default, configurable up to 240; a hard 12-hour lifetime stops even active codespaces. `gh codespace ssh` and Docker-in-Docker exist, but whether Console's normal SSH alias/agent works through the GitHub proxy is UNVERIFIED. Suitable for short experiments, not an unattended server; provisioning minutes, subject to quota. Set a stop-at-budget limit. [Allowance](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/reference/product-usage-included), [timeouts](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces/setting-your-user-preferences/setting-your-timeout-period-for-github-codespaces), [SSH](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces/developing-in-a-codespace/using-github-codespaces-with-github-cli), [Docker](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces/reference/allowing-your-codespace-to-access-a-private-registry).
- **Student Pack:** Nikhil `nikhilpravinpise` eligibility is **UNVERIFIED**; no private account was checked. The [current public offer list](https://education.github.com/pack) lists Azure $100 and Heroku "$13 USD per month for 24 months"; Heroku is an app platform, not a suitable controlled persistent SSH host. DigitalOcean is not listed on that page; an independently available current offer is UNVERIFIED. Student verification may take days.
- **Google Cloud Shell:** no fit: its VM is discarded after one hour of inactivity and only 5 GB home storage persists. [Official lifecycle](https://docs.cloud.google.com/shell/docs/how-cloud-shell-works).

All cloud estimates exclude optional domains, Claude subscription/API charges and overages. Do not select a paid upgrade, nonrefundable payment or chargeable resource; free-plan controls and actual prices must be confirmed in the provider UI.
